headlines: With two weeks until the midterms, more than 9 million Americans have already cast their ballots as Trump and both parties court undecided voters.
President Trump rallied supporters in Kansas and plans to campaign in seven more states in seven days as new polling shows voters disapprove of his handling of top issues.
Early voting began in Texas with Harris County breaking its first-day turnout record as Democrat James Talarico and Republican Ken Paxton held dueling rallies in the hotly contested Senate race.
Trump heads to North Carolina after rallying in Kansas, where Republican Senator Roger Marshall is fighting to hold his seat against Democrat Adam Hamilton in an unexpectedly tight race.
Trump used an anti-Semitic slur while defending Roger Marshall, a doctor who has sued patients with outstanding medical debts.
The Secret Service arrested a man in Kansas over the weekend for allegedly posting online about wanting to kill President Trump while he rallied in the state.

Democratic Texas governor candidate Gina Hinojosa filed a lawsuit seeking redacted documents about Governor Greg Abbott's emails with Elon Musk, calling them intimate and embarrassing; Abbott's spokesperson dismissed it as a baseless political stunt.

Michigan Senator Elissa Slotkin will travel to South Carolina to campaign for Democratic candidates ahead of the state's first-in-the-nation 2028 presidential primary, then head to Georgia to campaign with Senator Jon Ossoff.

Senate Minority Leader Chuck Schumer is pushing back on a conservative group's request that the FCC loosen robocall rules, warning candidates could use opponents' voices in misleading robocalls; the FCC says it does not plan to move forward with the change.

France saw its first calm night after the government imposed curfews and other restrictions in Paris and other cities to rein in violent large-scale protests, with thousands arrested over the weekend and new demonstrations set for Saturday.

A Florida state judge signed a new arrest warrant for former Cuban leader Raul Castro, and Florida's attorney general charged him with conspiracy to commit first-degree murder in the 1996 shootdown of two unarmed American civilian planes.

NBC legal analyst Misty Marris said it is highly unrealistic that 95-year-old Raul Castro, still in Cuba, will ever face trial in an American courtroom despite the open Florida warrant and existing federal charges.
The engine of a LATAM Airlines passenger jet caught fire just before takeoff in Lima, Peru, with all passengers evacuating safely and no one injured.
A private jet carrying actor Donnie Wahlberg skidded off the runway in Las Vegas and hit a perimeter fence while taking off for Canada; no one was injured.

A single-engine Cessna with engine failure nosedived into a busy San Jose, California street, narrowly missing homes; two adults and a child on board were expected to be okay and no one on the ground was hurt.

A nor'easter off the Carolinas is expected to bring coastal flooding, beach erosion and wind gusts near 40 mph to parts of the East Coast, while a slow-moving storm system threatens flash flooding in the Southwest.
The Tampa Bay Rays beat the Cleveland Guardians 7-3 in Game 6 to win the ALCS four games to two and reach the World Series for the third time in franchise history.
The Rays will face the Milwaukee Brewers in a World Series matchup guaranteeing a first-time champion, with Game 1 set for Friday.
President Trump campaigns through red states ahead of the midterm elections amid record-high fuel prices and record-low approval ratings.
Outrage grows over federal immigration agents' violent takedown of a U.S. citizen in Long Beach, California, that left his arm broken.
The NFL reportedly weighs in on the Eagles' handling of quarterback Jalen Hurts' blood clots in his lungs and legs, which sidelined him for the season.
Actress Christina Applegate reveals doctors misdiagnosed her with multiple sclerosis and says she is back at square one.
The Milwaukee Brewers will face the Tampa Bay Rays in the World Series, with both teams seeking their first title and both carrying bottom-half payrolls.
President Trump heads to North Carolina, where Democrat Roy Cooper leads Trump-backed former RNC chair Michael Whatley in a closely watched Senate race forecast as likely Democratic.
More than 13 million Americans have cast early ballots, with Georgia and parts of Texas seeing record-high voter turnout.
An Ohio governor's race attack ad featuring Democrat Amy Acton's estranged mother sparks anger from Democrats and Republicans, while Republican Vivek Ramaswamy declines to denounce it.
Republican Senate candidate Mike Rogers criticizes Trump's tariff war with Canada and urges continued support for Ukraine against Putin.
Democratic Senate candidate Abdul El-Sayed says attacks questioning his Muslim faith are an effort to paint him as an extremist.
The Justice Department threatens Los Angeles election officials with criminal charges if they don't set aside more than 20,000 ballots for review in its hunt for noncitizen voters.
The administration claims Pennsylvania, New Jersey and Nevada have thousands of noncitizen voters, but Nevada officials say they have found no noncitizen voters based on the information provided.

Long Beach Mayor Rex Richardson calls for an independent investigation into ICE's violent detention of U.S. citizen Ricardo Gonzalez and files a complaint with the Homeland Security inspector general.
Pending home sales fell to a 25-year low in September, dropping 7% from the prior month as mortgage rates climbed to about 7.4%.
A Russian drone strike near a Kyiv facility sends an ABC News team running to a bunker as attacks on Ukraine intensify.
President Trump pressures Ukrainian President Zelensky to make a deal with Russia, while Ukraine says U.S. intelligence sharing was briefly interrupted before being restored.
The Wall Street Journal reports Elon Musk personally ordered a slowdown of the military version of Starlink, limiting Ukraine's drone capabilities.
The NFL reportedly decides the Eagles will not be punished over their handling of Jalen Hurts' blood clots.
A neurologist explains that up to 20% of MS cases can be misdiagnosed and discusses how doctors are working to determine what is causing Christina Applegate's symptoms.
The former Cornell student who alleges she was gang-raped at a fraternity house says she felt unsupported and disbelieved by university president Michael Kotlikoff.
AI company Anthropic, maker of Claude, reportedly had a net loss of more than $80 billion in the first half of the year.
France's prime minister announces a massive security presence for next weekend in anticipation of new protests following nationwide demonstrations that turned to vandalism.
Kyle Kennedy, a grandchild of Bobby and Ethel Kennedy, has died at age 42 after suffering a severe spinal cord injury in 2020.
The band U2 will perform at the halftime show of the NFL's first-ever Thanksgiving Eve game between the Green Bay Packers and Los Angeles Rams.
A Dirty Dancing sequel is in the works with Jennifer Grey expected to reprise her role as Baby, and producers say they will not use AI to bring back Patrick Swayze's character.
Amazon is adding 50,000 holiday season jobs this year, paying seasonal employees $20 an hour.
Nearly $1 million worth of Pokémon cards were stolen from a FedEx truck in California.
Cardi B performed an eight-song, 19-minute set for NPR's Tiny Desk, drawing more than 2 million views in under 24 hours.
More than 100 dachshunds from around the world competed in the fourth annual dachshund race in Munich, Germany.
Comedian Katt Williams discusses his debut memoir, Nine Lives, No Wives and 69 Concubines, and his path from running away from home at 13 to owning his own movie studio.
At least four civilians killed and 27 wounded in another night of Russian drone and missile attacks on Ukraine.
A Russian drone strike on a park in Ukraine's northeastern Kharkiv region killed six people, including three children.
Finland's government announced it would purchase 1 million anti-personnel landmines for more than $100 million after withdrawing from the mine ban treaty.
Russia is accused of opening a new front in its hybrid war against Ukraine after a Russian satellite made an uninvited rendezvous with a Finnish-American radar satellite used by Ukraine's military.
President Trump said it is time for somebody else to negotiate on behalf of Ukraine and criticized President Zelensky.
President Zelensky met with US special envoy Steve Witkoff in Norway, with Jared Kushner joining remotely, as Zelensky said Ukraine has nearly run out of Patriot interceptors.
A drone strike near a market in Sudan's West Kordofan State killed 80 people, one of the deadliest single strikes since the war began in April 2023.
President Trump campaigned in Park City, Kansas, for Republican Senator Roger Marshall, who faces Democrat Adam Hamilton.
A New York Times review found Senator Roger Marshall sued more than 700 of his own patients over unpaid medical bills, leading to 81 arrests.
President Trump defended Senator Marshall for suing his patients while using an anti-Semitic slur.
CBS News chief legal correspondent Jan Crawford apologized for a social media post praising a man who heckled Democratic Senate candidate Dr. Abdul El-Sayed at a Michigan town hall.

Dropsite News reported Republican Senate candidate Mike Rogers' personal wealth soared after 2011 due to his marriage to Aegis executive Kristi Clemens Rogers, whose firm landed billions in contracts during his tenure.
The Intercept reported Mike Rogers spent more than $100,000 last quarter on chartered flights, a Miami car service, and BMW repairs.

Mexican lawful permanent resident Emiliano Andrade Covarrubias was found dead in his cell at the Rio Grande Processing Center in Laredo, Texas, the seventh person to die in ICE custody in Texas this year.
ICE agents broke the arm of US citizen Ricardo Gonzalez during a protest in Long Beach, California.

Mississippi's Attorney General ruled a police officer was justified in fatally shooting 1-year-old Corbin Wylie, who was killed in a Walmart parking lot after police responded to a report of shoplifting.
Palestinian activist and Columbia graduate Mahmoud Khalil asked the US Supreme Court to overturn a ruling that enabled the Trump administration to re-arrest and deport him.
Protesters rallied outside Meta's corporate offices in São Paulo, Brazil, accusing the company of electoral interference ahead of Sunday's runoff election between Lula da Silva and Flávio Bolsonaro.
